text:
Marathon Petroleum stock rose modestly today, gaining 0.83%, but the bigger story is the sharp 10% drop it's taken over the past week. That decline reflects a collapse in refining margins driven by falling crude prices—US oil dropped from roughly $115 per barrel two weeks ago to $89.50 today—combined with weak downstream demand signals. Even though refineries are running hot at 95.7% capacity and storage levels remain relatively normal, lower oil prices squeeze what refiners can earn by processing crude into gasoline and diesel.

The escalating geopolitical tension in the Middle East—Iran's attacks on US positions in Kuwait and warnings that the Strait of Hormuz is no longer a reliable energy corridor—creates a paradox for the refining sector. While supply disruptions typically support oil prices and refiner margins, the market has instead repriced lower on recession concerns and demand weakness, leaving refiners caught between constrained margins and rising geopolitical risk.
